clue.text: Flyer's transport almost late

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for late is not reached

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: A pilot complains that the vehicle bringing them to the airfield is nearly late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large heavy bird that can fly, so it is a flyer.

clue.text: Rudely kissed bosom is reported

indicators.note: reported means we take the word for bosom as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: bust means bosom

explanation.surface: A tabloid tells of someone kissed roughly on the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST and BUSSED sound the same; 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To buss is an old, informal verb for kissing loudly or heartily.

clue.text: Power cut all round makes a prominent story

indicators.note: all round means the word for cut surrounds the letter for power

parts.note: slash means cut
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A power cut affecting everyone becomes front-page news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cut' reads as one phrase, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a splash is the main headline story spread across a front page.

clue.text: Self-directing car without computer control wasting energy

parts.note: auto is a car
no means without, as in 'no sugar'

indicators.note: wasting means the energy letter is lost from the computer device

parts.note: a mouse is a device for controlling a computer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A self-driving car that needs no computer control and burns no fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomous means self-governing, acting independently without outside control.

clue.text: Work for two that five divide fairly makes such a day for relaxing

indicators.note: dividing fairly splits the duo's piece exactly down the middle, where the numeral goes

parts.note: a duet is a piece of music for two performers
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A shared task split fairly makes for an easy day off.
explanation.walkthrough: A duvet day is a British phrase for a day off taken to stay in bed or relax; the definition is the answer as that phrase's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet day is an informal day off spent resting, so the quilt names that kind of lazy day.

clue.text: Friend shot back in very old British language

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British

indicators.note: shot back means the word for friend is sent the other way

parts.note: pal means friend

explanation.surface: A friend fires back in some quaint old British dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Volapük is an artificial language devised in 1879, a forerunner of Esperanto.
explanation.definitionFit: Volapük is a constructed international language, invented by Johann Martin Schleyer.

clue.text: Garment, one sort of blue, that may be inside the front door

definitions.text: that may be inside the front door

parts.note: a vest is a garment
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sort of means the letters of blue are rearranged into another sort

explanation.surface: A garment in a shade of blue, which you might hang just inside the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall or lobby just inside a building's outer door.

clue.text: Speed to defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a fast pace, as in 'at a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses share a word with no link between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lick is both an informal noun for a rapid pace and an informal verb for beating an opponent.

clue.text: Pub notice laid out in this funny-looking alphabet

definitions.note: an alphabet that is phonetic; the answer is the adjective

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

indicators.note: laid out means the letters of notice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice in a pub written in some strange-looking script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub notice' looks like one item to shuffle, but the pub gives only PH.
explanation.definitionFit: The International Phonetic Alphabet uses odd symbols to record speech sounds, so it looks strange.

clue.text: After opener stumped, single that is vital to stability

parts.note: a key opens a lock
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
one means single

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: after the opening batter is stumped, one run steadies the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just says which pieces come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone at the top of an arch that holds the others in place.

clue.text: Light snow covers large crack

indicators.note: covers means the light snow word goes around the letter for large

parts.note: to spit is to fall in light scattered drops or flakes
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A light dusting of snow hides a big crack in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a crack or fissure, as in a split in wood.

clue.text: Urn, not too big, cost nothing: goodness, a snip

parts.note: a vase is an urn-like vessel

indicators.note: not means the outsize letters are taken out of the word cost

parts.note: taken as written before letters are removed
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for too big
O is zero, nothing
my is an exclamation like goodness

explanation.surface: An urn, not too big, came free: goodness, a bargain!
explanation.walkthrough: 'a snip' poses as a bargain, but it means the surgical cut. Removing O and S from COST leaves CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vasectomy is informally called the snip, the minor operation cutting the sperm ducts.

clue.text: Film director a genius to include heartless scene

indicators.note: to include means the genius's name takes the remaining letters inside it

parts.note: Einstein is the byword for a genius

indicators.note: heartless means all the inner letters of scene are removed

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A film director, a true genius, includes a cold-blooded scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' suggests cruelty, but here it strips a word to its outer letters. Sergei Eisenstein directed Battleship Potemkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet filmmaker famous for Battleship Potemkin and montage editing.

clue.text: Strengthening border means the world to a German

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reinforcing strip or edging on a shoe or garment

definitions.text: means the world to a German
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the German word for world

explanation.walkthrough: 'means the world to' sounds like affection; it is a literal translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A welt is a stitched reinforcing seam, and in German Welt is the noun for world.

clue.text: Small version of me squeezed up in so-called convertible

indicators.note: squeezed means the turned pronoun is pressed into the other letters
in places the turned pronoun inside the rearranged letters
convertible means these letters can be changed into another order

parts.note: the letters of so-called are the fodder

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means me reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a miniature of themselves squashed into a toy convertible car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' reads as a car, but it is the anagram signal, and 'so-called' is fodder rather than a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale model is a smaller replica built in exact proportion to the original.

clue.text: See 17
Passionate desire reproved, having to be purified

parts.note: lust is passionate desire
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold, so rated means reproved

explanation.surface: Someone's lust is scolded and must be cleansed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' meaning scold is old-fashioned; 'having to be' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to cleanse ceremonially, a ritual purification.

clue.text: Small country lane initially badly laid across island

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of lane

parts.note: only its first letter is used
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
I is the map abbreviation for island
put means laid, placed

explanation.surface: A country lane, poorly surfaced, runs across an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' just strings the pieces along in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput is the land of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels, so a small country indeed.

clue.text: Bore draw possibly? It could be an unexpected revelation

definitions.text: It could be an unexpected revelation

parts.note: these two words are what you get when the answer's first word has its letters jumbled, with the second word acting as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A dull goalless draw, perhaps, and then something surprising is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: MALFUNCTION signals an anagram of WARDROBE, which gives BORE DRAW; 'possibly' warns that the clue words are an example of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a euphemism for clothing slipping and accidentally exposing the body in public.

clue.text: Belonging to a teaching organisation is ghastly, to be brief

parts.note: in means belonging to, as in 'in the club'
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
's is the short form of is
hell, as in 'it's hell', means something ghastly

explanation.surface: Being a member of a teachers' union is awful, to put it shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers; IN A NUT'S HELL reads as 'in a union is hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in summary, concisely, using the fewest words.

clue.text: Hateful to be overdrawn — one's recourse?

parts.note: OD is the bank statement abbreviation for overdrawn
IOUs, written promises to pay, are the recourse of someone short of money

explanation.surface: Being overdrawn is hateful, and is one left only with promises to pay?
explanation.walkthrough: IOU stands for 'I owe you'; 'to be' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means detestable, arousing strong dislike.

clue.text: Like a bird at the back

parts.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Something bird-like sits behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for behind or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Cover over pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone covers over the swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Agreed to smash one of the old gods that screw man

indicators.note: to smash means the word for agreed breaks into the god's name

parts.note: Ares was the Greek god of war
chimed means agreed, as in 'chimed with'

explanation.surface: Followers agree to destroy an ancient god associated with a screw.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archimedes screw is a device for raising water, named after the Greek mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes is credited with inventing the water-lifting screw that bears his name.

clue.text: One plucked posy in the end for rapacious monster

parts.note: a harp is an instrument whose strings are plucked

indicators.note: in the end means take the final letter of posy

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone plucks a little bunch of flowers, ending up with a greedy monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucked' suggests flowers picked for the posy; it is a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpies were grasping winged monsters in Greek myth, half woman and half bird.

clue.text: Make coffee and get a tip

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a perquisite or gratuity, such as a tip

explanation.walkthrough: 'and get a' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Perk is short for percolate when brewing, and for perquisite, an extra benefit or gratuity.

clue.text: Guardian's right for a time for deputy head

indicators.note: for means the letter for right stands in place of the letter for time

parts.note: a protector is a guardian
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A newspaper has turned right for a while, becoming a mere deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is just a protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A prorector is a deputy rector, the vice-head of a university or college.

clue.text: Urged peace-lover to embrace end of war

indicators.note: to embrace means the peace-lover's word goes around that letter

parts.note: a dove is someone who favours peace

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of war

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A pacifist pressed for a hug to end the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Drove means pushed or forced on, as in driving cattle.

clue.text: Changed a little feeble content in series of talks

indicators.note: content in means the word for feeble is what the talks contain

parts.note: TED is the conference brand famous for its series of short talks
weak means feeble

explanation.surface: Some feeble material in a lecture series got minor edits.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make a small adjustment.

clue.text: Boris going out in style

indicators.note: going out suggests leaving in a dramatic way, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Boris leaves in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris' suggests Johnson; it is Boris Yeltsin, Russia's first president.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was President of Russia in the 1990s, so his first name serves as a definition by example.
